newsitem.title: USA: Republican lawmaker warns Clinton on Medicare.
newsitem.headline: Republican lawmaker warns Clinton on Medicare.

text.p: An influential Republican lawmaker said Friday President Clinton would have to take the lead on Medicare reform and Republicans would not allow him to push off the hard parts on a nonpartisan commission.

In a sharply worded speech to a business group, California Republican Bill Thomas, chairman of the health subcommittee of the Ways and Means Committee, criticised Clinton for "demagoguing" the Medicare debate for political gain during his re-election campaign.

He said Republicans, whose sweeping plans to overhaul Medicare and significantly slow spending were stalled during last year's budget battles, would now let Clinton take the lead -- and take the political heat.

"We are going to have to make changes in these programmes. But it is now the president who is going to have to sell these programmes," Thomas said. "The Republicans look forward to the president offering his specific proposals to quote, unquote, fix Medicare."

He said Republicans opposed new taxes for Medicare or using accounting gimmicks to shift expenses around. He did not rule out a commission to deal with aspects of Medicare reform but opposed a short-term fix, leaving all the difficult parts to a long-term panel of experts whose recommendations would not necessarily be followed.

"What's happened has happened. My lament is over the fact that it's now going to be more difficult to do what we have to do," he said. "The reason it's more difficult is because of the 'Medigoguery' the president to the last minute engaged in (during his re-election campaign)."

Medicare's hospital trust fund is heading for bankrupty in 2001. Republicans and Democrats alike want to restrain spending in the other portions of Medicare as they strive to balance the federal budget, although Republicans have advocated steeper restraints than the Democrats.
Founded in 1965, Medicare provides health coverage to around 38 million Americans -- everyone over age 65 and certain disabled people.
